## e282a664f807

**Classification: reproduced defect.** Generator SHA-256 `833974efcb937161a77545a63e6fa5cec73b8d948436c5a18cfb370317abf64b`.

The rule selects the unique nonzero color occurring twice and fills the rectangle bounded by those cells. The ordinary sampler always writes the pair northwest-to-southeast. A plausible wrong rule is therefore: “fill the bounding box only when the repeated pair has positive slope; otherwise output blank.”

`checks/audit/e282a664f807_probe.json` measured 200 draws in each of `None`, `easy`, `medium`, and `hard` (800 total), with seed `282000 + index` and sample index `11*index + 3`. All 800 pairs had positive slope; the wrong rule matched the intended bbox output on 800/800, and every generated input passed `self_check`.

Canonical pair index 2 has the repeated color 6 at `(1,6)` and `(5,2)`, a negative slope. It is validator-lawful. The supported Racket output fills rows 1–5 and columns 2–6 with 6; the rival returns an all-zero output and disagrees. Exact input, hashes, validator result, authority output, rival output, and command are retained in `checks/audit/e282a664f807/finding.json`; raw supported-CLI evidence is in `checks/audit/e282a664f807/racket.json`.

A second concrete contract defect is independently reproduced: `AXES['box_height']` advertises `1..8`, but `generate(1, 0, box_height=1)` raises `ValueError: draw_int('box_height'): override 1 outside [2, 6]`. This is recorded in the probe JSON. No source was changed.
